limitations: In-process single-client pilot. Exact sources, synchronized query receipts and packet serialization are timed; hosting and out-of-RAM operation are unmeasured.
The large tool I/O and opaque payload are public deterministic synthetic fixtures; real private raw tool outputs are not imported.

Public tracked source files are chunked at approximately 8 KiB without overlap, with exact offsets and complete-file reconstruction checks. Raw tool records remain stored and have linked passage copies.

Tool cases use controlled synthetic clocks and include an old/new output revision. Public distractors use timestamp zero solely for the stress test; these are not verified historical availability times.
SQLite uses its global FTS5 term statistics with indexed historical/latest eligibility predicates. Nine computes query-relative historical statistics. Neither result cache is used.

Source retention is measured against fixed quotes. Symbol lookups are mechanical code-search probes; the reused engineering-history pilot is small and not held out. No generated-answer accuracy or actual answer-model token count is measured.
The larger candidate pool and context budgets are explicit controls, not a ranking-algorithm improvement. The same passage construction benefits both engines.
Archive bytes exclude the Nine RAM index; SQLite source/FTS size excludes its separate durable benchmark receipt journal. Source text includes duplicated raw-tool and passage representations.
